title: Debiasing Learning for Membership Inference Attacks Against Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Recommender systems may leak information about their training data, creating privacy risks addressed through membership inference attacks.

gap.claim: Existing attack methods face bias from differences between shadow and target recommenders and inaccurate difference-vector estimation because hidden recommender states are not observable.

contributions.claim: The work investigates privacy threats to recommender systems using membership inference as the analytical lens.
The work identifies two challenges affecting membership inference attacks against recommender systems: biased attack-model training data and inaccurate difference-vector estimates.

narrative_sequence.summary: Training-data leakage by learned recommender systems can create privacy violations.
The paper studies recommender-system privacy threats through membership inference, where an adversary determines whether a user's data trained the target recommender.
Prior attacks use a shadow recommender to generate attack-model training data and compare historical interactions with recommended items using difference vectors.
Existing methods are challenged by shadow-target mismatch and unobservable hidden recommender states.

source_observation.claim: Attack-model training data derived from a shadow recommender can be biased when the shadow and target recommenders differ.

interpretation.claim: Surrogate-system mismatch can distort privacy-attack behavior.

application.claim: Evaluate membership-inference methods for sensitivity to differences between surrogate and target systems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which differences matter or how sensitivity should be measured.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the proposed debiasing method.
The abstract does not report datasets, baselines, metrics, quantitative results, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported challenges.
